doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Today's singers and bookings
summary: He complains that modern singers shout rather than sing, unlike the big band singers he grew up with.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: So are you still pretty - you keep pretty current with what these artists are doing today, just to - what their artistic output is?

Oh yeah, yeah. There are a lot of them that I guess we could bring in that would bring a lot of people in, but the music isn’t there. It’s all BS as far as I’m concerned. We have eight million singers who want to come in that can’t sing. They all just holler and scream and all that. And I grew up with big band singers where they stood in one place, they sang, you understood the lyrics, they were in tune, and they work with the band. Now they dance all over the stage, they holler and scream, and blah blah blah. Forget about it.
